solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Paid athletes training by court in Panorama (8)

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation, as in a street address

annotation.surface: Professional players are put through their paces at a court with a fine view.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Panorama' sits at the end looking like the setting for the training, but it is the definition; 'in' is only a link.
annotation.definitionFit: A prospect is a wide view of a landscape, which is what a panorama is.

entries.clue: Writer getting call at work in office building (8)

blocks.note: to tag is to call or label something
a machine that is working is on

annotation.surface: An author takes a phone call while working in an office block.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like a person but is the pen; 'getting' just joins the pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: The Pentagon is the famous five-sided headquarters of the US Defense Department, an office building.

entries.clue: Batch of deliveries on time, but open (5)

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or 'delivered'

annotation.surface: A load of parcels turns up on schedule, but its packaging is open.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about parcel deliveries; the deliveries are really a bowler's, and six of them make a cricket over.
annotation.definitionFit: Overt means done in the open, not hidden.

entries.clue: Go mad in a pub to the south on the lash (4,3,4,3)

indicatorNotes.on the lash: someone on the lash is out getting drunk, so the letters are staggering about

annotation.surface: Someone goes wild on a drinking spree at a pub down south.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the lash' is British slang for out on a heavy drinking session. The whole surface is a night out, which suits the answer's sense of splashing out.
annotation.definitionFit: To push the boat out is to spend lavishly on a celebration, going a bit mad with money.

entries.clue: Loud noise beginning to chafe film director (5)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A loud noise starts to irritate a film director on set.
annotation.walkthrough: Fritz Lang was the German director of Metropolis and M.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though narrower: the word names the ringing sound of struck metal, one particular loud noise.

entries.clue: A little amount of bread to be picked up (4)

indicatorNotes.to be picked up: a sound is picked up by the ear

blocks.note: bread is slang for money, and a sum is an amount of money

annotation.surface: A small quantity of bread is waiting to be collected.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is money, not a loaf, so 'amount of bread' is a sum. 'A little' is the definition, as in 'have some'.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Some' and 'a little' both mean a modest quantity: have some milk, have a little milk.

entries.clue: Coach turning right in old place like Morocco, say (9)

indicatorNotes.turning: a thing turned round faces the other way, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.in: R goes inside the old word for place

blocks.note: a coach is a long-distance bus
topic once meant a place, from Greek topos

annotation.surface: A coach tour turns right into some old town in a country like Morocco.
annotation.walkthrough: TOPIC in its obsolete sense means a place (Greek topos); R goes into it to make TROPIC. 'Say' marks Morocco as one example of a subtropical country.
annotation.definitionFit: Morocco lies just north of the Tropic of Cancer, so its climate is subtropical.

entries.clue: Upstanding Barnet medical officer seen with warmonger (6)

blocks.note: a hawk is a politician who favours war

annotation.surface: A respectable doctor from Barnet, the London suburb, is spotted with someone itching for war.
annotation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London borough, but also rhyming slang: 'Barnet Fair' = hair. Upstanding hair is a Mohawk, the spiky strip of hair down the middle of the head.
annotation.definitionFit: A Mohawk is a hairstyle whose central strip of hair stands straight up.

entries.clue: Important cause represented in unrealistic drama (5,2,1,6)

indicatorNotes.represented: the letters are presented again in a new form

annotation.surface: A worthy cause is portrayed in a far-fetched play.
annotation.walkthrough: The irony is the point: an 'important cause' rearranges into a fuss about nothing.
annotation.definitionFit: A storm in a teacup is a great fuss over something trivial, drama out of all proportion to reality.

entries.clue: Ligue 1 side taking lead from Scottish Premiership side (6)

indicatorNotes.taking lead from: the lead, or first letter, is taken away

blocks.note: RANGERS without its first letter R

annotation.surface: A French football club signs a star player from a Scottish club.
annotation.walkthrough: Ligue 1 is France's top football division, and Angers SCO plays in it. Rangers is one of Glasgow's two big clubs.
annotation.definitionFit: Angers is a French town whose football club, Angers SCO, plays in Ligue 1.

entries.clue: Utahan criminal bored by old black German’s way (8)

indicatorNotes.criminal: a criminal twists things, so the letters are bent out of order
indicatorNotes.bored by: the rearranged letters are drilled through by O and B, which end up inside

annotation.surface: A crooked man from Utah is being bored by an old black German's way of doing things.
annotation.walkthrough: A Utahan is someone from Utah. 'German's way' reads as a German's manner, but it is a literal road.
annotation.definitionFit: An Autobahn is a German motorway, a German's way in the sense of a road.

entries.clue: Pack of hams and pickles finally eaten by pet (4)

indicatorNotes.finally: the final letter of the word
indicatorNotes.eaten by: S goes inside CAT, as food goes inside the eater

annotation.surface: A cat wolfs down a packet of ham and some pickles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hams' are not meat but overacting actors, so a pack of hams is a whole troupe of them. The deli surface hides that entirely.
annotation.definitionFit: A cast is the full group of actors in a production; hams are bad actors.

entries.clue: Wig partner adjusted for one in a shell suit? (5,5)

indicatorNotes.adjusted: the letters are adjusted into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone straightens their partner's wig before going out in a shiny tracksuit.
annotation.walkthrough: A shell suit is a garish nylon tracksuit popular in 1980s Britain; the question mark lets it mean a literal shell worn as a suit.
annotation.definitionFit: A tiger prawn is a large prawn, a creature that lives inside its own shell.

entries.clue: Mill around with noble cop and reactionary (7,5)

annotation.surface: A crowd mills about with an aristocrat, a policeman and a die-hard conservative.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mill around' reads as one phrase meaning to drift about, but MILL is fodder and 'around' is the instruction. Colonel Blimp was a pompous cartoon character from 1930s Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: Colonel Blimp became the byword for a pompous, reactionary old Englishman.
annotation.definitionNote: The definition is an adjective used as a noun: a reactionary person.

entries.clue: Celebs on broadcast ultimately showy in a rude way (9)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: the letters are scattered widely, like seed

annotation.surface: Celebrities on TV end up showing off crudely.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' pretends to be about television, which suits 'celebs', but it is scattering the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Obscenely means in an indecent or offensive way, which is rude.

entries.clue: Haul up fish of a low standard (3)

indicatorNotes.Haul up: in a down clue, hauling a word up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a dab is a small flatfish

annotation.surface: An angler reels in a fish that is not up to much.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Haul up' fits the fishing picture, but in a down entry it turns DAB upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of poor quality, as in a bad film or a bad job.

entries.clue: Foreigner with men navy captured close to Ibiza (8)

indicatorNotes.captured: RN takes A prisoner inside itself
indicatorNotes.close to: the close, or last letter, of the word

blocks.note: OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

annotation.surface: An outsider arrives along with sailors who took a Spanish island.
annotation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is the usual crossword source for 'men'. Andorra sits in the Pyrenees, not far from Ibiza's Spain, which keeps the surface on topic.
annotation.definitionFit: An Andorran, from Andorra, is a foreigner to a British solver.

entries.clue: Steps to be taken over bladed weapons? (5,7)

annotation.definition: Steps to be taken over bladed weapons?

blocks.note: the surface wants official measures or action; the setter means dance steps
the surface wants 'concerning weapons'; the setter means physically over swords laid on the floor

annotation.surface: It reads like a policy of measures to be taken about knife crime.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Steps to be taken' sounds like official measures on weapons; in fact they are dance steps, placed over swords laid on the floor, as in the Scottish sword dance.
annotation.definitionFit: Sword dancing involves stepping nimbly over crossed swords on the ground.

entries.clue: Event celebrating Shakespeare perhaps is OK (4,2)

blocks.note: William Shakespeare, known as Will; 'perhaps' marks him as one example
a do is a party or celebratory event

annotation.surface: A festival honouring Shakespeare is given approval.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'a DO for WILL', so the pieces come out in the reverse of clue order.
annotation.definitionFit: 'That will do' means that is acceptable, OK.
annotation.definitionNote: The answer is a phrase with its own verb, matching 'is OK'.

entries.clue: Some blockhead I let tan tenor’s an amateur (10)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters of the phrase are used

annotation.surface: An idiot lets a singer sunbathe, and the tenor turns out to be a mere amateur.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A dilettante dabbles in an art without professional commitment: an amateur.

entries.clue: Knight covered with no clothes at front is thus (5)

indicatorNotes.at front: the C at the front of CAKED is what goes missing

blocks.note: N = knight in chess notation, since K is the king
caked in mud = covered in it
CAKED without its first letter, the C of 'clothes'

annotation.surface: A knight wearing nothing but a coat of mud is in the altogether.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thus' points back at the whole picture: a knight with no clothes is naked, so the clue is half its own definition. 'No clothes at front' strips the C (first of 'clothes') off CAKED.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Thus' means in the state just described, and a knight with no clothes is naked.

entries.clue: Scream from gangster making duke tense (4)

indicatorNotes.making: to make a duke tense is to turn him into it, so one letter is swapped for another
indicatorNotes.tense: tense is the grammar term abbreviated T, and it is what the duke's D is made into

blocks.note: d = duke, t = tense: the D of HOOD becomes T

annotation.surface: A gangster screams while turning a duke into a nervous wreck.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scream' is the noun meaning something hilarious, not a shriek.
annotation.definitionFit: A hoot and a scream both mean a very funny person or thing.

entries.clue: Do not top or tail tongue (5)

indicatorNotes.not top or tail: the top and tail are the first and last letters, both removed

blocks.note: a do is a party, a shindig

annotation.surface: An order not to trim a joint of meat at either end, or to eat the tongue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Do not' reads as a command, but 'Do' is the party noun and 'not top or tail' strips its ends.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: 'tongue' in its sense of a language, and Hindi, the main language of northern India, is one.

entries.clue: Erotic pleasure gets king in cold sweat (4,4)

blocks.note: a blue film is an erotic one

annotation.surface: A king's guilty pleasure leaves him in a cold sweat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gets' just adds K to BLUE FUN.
annotation.definitionFit: A blue funk is a state of panic or terror, the kind that brings on a cold sweat.

entries.clue: Unknown artist seen about with cooler singer (6)

indicatorNotes.seen about: about means turned around, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the cooler and the can are both slang for prison

annotation.surface: An obscure painter is spotted about town with a chilled drinks box and a vocalist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' is prison slang. 'Singer' works twice over: the songbird, and criminal slang for an informer who sings to the police.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the canary is kept for its song, and in underworld slang a canary is also an informer who sings.

entries.clue: Flipping rubbish start for young right-winger (4)

indicatorNotes.Flipping: the word is flipped over, reading backwards
indicatorNotes.start for: the start of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: An exasperated 'flipping rubbish!' greets a young Conservative starting out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swear word before it does its job of reversing ROT. A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Britain's Conservative Party sits on the right, so any of its members is a right-winger.

entries.clue: A choice about head of department taking over? (8)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' in its sense of around: the phrase 'A choice' wraps around the letter that follows
indicatorNotes.head of: the head of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A decision about who heads the department when it is taken over.
annotation.walkthrough: The office surface suggests a corporate takeover; the question mark signals that 'taking over' means taking on a child as your own.
annotation.definitionFit: Adoption is taking over responsibility for a child, or taking up an idea as your own.
